label: GO after an unrewarded trial, late in the episode, when the agent strongly commits to a2
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only in episode trials ~70-99 (none before 60), almost exclusively when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward 0, or a -1 penalty after a D1 fixation error) and the policy strongly prefers a2 (choice logit < -8.9, model_act = 2; 97% of mass in the lowest choice decile). Value is low (all activations below the 7.13 value quantile). In practice the previous trial is usually a2 -> S1 rare unrewarded (prev_common = 0 holds 83% of mass), i.e. a model-based stay on a2 after a rare loss, with S2 good; adding prev_common != 1 barely changes F1 (0.822 vs 0.817), so it was left out. Does not fire after rewarded trials, at a1 choices, or early in the episode. Highest activations come where all conditions hold (top quartile coverage ~1.0); weak activations are the misses with milder a2 preference. All variables are observed or the agent own policy output; no future variables used. Dev: P 0.77, R 0.88, F1 0.82, mass recall 0.97.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: the claimed onset at trial 70 is wrong. The feature ramps up between trials 70 and 79. For predicate-true GO steps, the per-trial precision is 0.02 at trial 70, 0.04 at 71, 0.07 at 72, 0.13 at 73, 0.22 at 74, 0.24 at 75, 0.44 at 76, 0.56 at 77, 0.84 at 78 and 0.91 at 79, then about 0.98 or higher from trial 80 on. Most of the predicate's roughly 2500 test false positives come from trials 70-75 (precision 0.09 in the 70-74 bin).

Moving the cutoff to ep_trial >= 76 raises dev F1 from 0.817 to 0.890 and test F1 from 0.801 to 0.871. Precision goes from 0.76 to 0.93, recall drops only from 0.84 to 0.82, and mass recall stays at 0.95. So 'late in the episode (>= 70)' overstates the trials where the feature is active.

The explanation gets the -1 penalty wrong. A previous-trial -1 penalty (prev_reward == -1) has only 1 activation in 51 steps. The real pattern is a D1 fixation error in the CURRENT trial, seen as in_rew = -1 at GO: 394 of 492 such steps are active (80%, 98x lift), and d1_err == 1 has 28% firing. Those steps still satisfy the predicate because their prev_reward is 0 or 1 as usual.
Minor: 'does not fire after rewarded trials' is nearly true. There are 450 activations after a rewarded trial, but they hold only 0.4% of the mass.

Claims that check out: the feature fires only at GO (0 activations at D1 or D2), only on a2 with model_act 2, only with value below 7.13, and 97% of its mass is at choice < -8.91. prev_common == 1 adds almost nothing (108 predicted steps), so leaving out a rare-transition condition is fine. The predicate uses no future variables.
